slides.title: Chat feels like the playground
slides.text: Chatting in a game can feel like the playground, full of friends and jokes. But a screen hides who is really typing, so chat needs its own safety rules.
slides.alt: Would you rather put class work on a page anyone can comment on, or a page only your class can see?

focus.cue: A class page where anyone can comment
A class page only your class can see

slides.title: People you know in real life
slides.text: Safe chat is for people you know in real life: family, classmates and friends you have met face to face. A friendly stranger online is still a stranger.
slides.alt: Would you rather use a nickname nobody can trace to you, or your real first name so friends can find you?

focus.cue: Chat with a nickname nobody can trace
Or your real name, for strangers to find

slides.title: Never move to a private chat
slides.text: A safe player never moves to a private chat because someone asks. That request is a warning sign, and so is any chat that must stay secret from trusted adults.
slides.alt: A trick card from someone you do not know: it fishes for the street a player lives on.

focus.cue: A new friend asks for your street and offers a gift
A new friend: an unknown sender

slides.title: Spot the warning signs
slides.text: A new player in your game chat is very friendly, then asks two things. A Defender reads the signs before answering.
steps: They ask which school you go to
They ask you to move to a private chat
Leave the chat and tell a trusted adult
slides.alt: A trick card from someone you do not know: it fishes for the street a player lives on.

focus.cue: Asks where you live; someone you have never met
The safe move: ask a trusted adult

slides.title: Leaving is a lock
slides.text: You may leave any chat at any time, for any reason. Blocking someone who worries you is not rude. Blocking is a lock, and locks are what Defenders do.
slides.alt: A third trick card: the safe move is always the same — stop, do not reply, and tell a trusted adult.

focus.cue: A message you may leave at any time
Decide calmly: leaving a chat is always allowed

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Play Would You Rather first: choose the Online topic and play Online: share or keep. Talk through each chat choice before you pick a side.
slides.alt: A Would You Rather online dilemma: something you made, and the choice of whether to share it or keep it.
